children.name: The blue heart
children.__text: Every world beginswith a little light.

children.name: System introduction
children.__text: One blue hypergiant. Three extraordinary planets. One silent moon. A journey through a system that exists only beyond imagination.

children.name: Fictional universe note
children.__text: A FICTIONAL UNIVERSE. A REAL SENSE OF WONDER.

children.name: Fabre statement
children.__text: Where the ocean learned to glow.

children.name: Fabre description
children.__text: An endless cobalt sea, threaded with living light. Beneath Fabre’s pearl-white storms, luminous reef forests follow the slow pulse of Aetherium across the water.

children.name: Fabre observation note
children.__text: At night, the shoreline becomes a constellation of its own.

backgroundImage.altText: Fabre, a sapphire ocean planet with luminous coastlines.
Jaunes, a turquoise gas giant with immense swirling storms.

children.name: Jaunes statement
children.__text: A world without a still moment.

children.name: Jaunes description
children.__text: Teal cloud rivers circle a world with no solid shore. On Jaunes, a single storm can outlive a civilisation, turning beneath rings of suspended ice and mineral dust.

children.name: Jaunes observation note
children.__text: The Great Spiral has been turning for 9,000 years.

children.name: Devis description
children.__text: At the edge of the blue light lies Devis, a pale archive of the system’s first winter. Vast crystalline plains conceal a dark, warm ocean beneath forty kilometres of ice.

children.name: Devis observation note
children.__text: A frozen surface. An unexpected world underneath.

backgroundImage.altText: Devis, a white ice world split by blue crystalline fissures.

children.name: Indy description
children.__text: Indy keeps a quiet watch over Devis. Silver impact basins hold ancient blue ice, and its slow, synchronised orbit always offers the same scarred face to the planet it calls home.

children.name: Indy observation note
children.__text: The smallest world in our atlas. The oldest stories.

backgroundImage.altText: Indy, the silver cratered moon of Devis.

children.name: The blue heart
children.__text: Every world beginswith a little light.

children.name: System introduction
children.__text: One blue hypergiant. Three extraordinary planets. One silent moon. A journey through a system that exists only beyond imagination.

children.name: Fictional universe note
children.__text: A FICTIONAL UNIVERSE. A REAL SENSE OF WONDER.

children.name: Fabre statement
children.__text: Where the ocean learned to glow.

children.name: Fabre description
children.__text: An endless cobalt sea, threaded with living light. Beneath Fabre’s pearl-white storms, luminous reef forests follow the slow pulse of Aetherium across the water.

children.name: Fabre observation note
children.__text: At night, the shoreline becomes a constellation of its own.

backgroundImage.altText: Fabre, a sapphire ocean planet with luminous coastlines.
Jaunes, a turquoise gas giant with immense swirling storms.

children.name: Jaunes statement
children.__text: A world without a still moment.

children.name: Jaunes description
children.__text: Teal cloud rivers circle a world with no solid shore. On Jaunes, a single storm can outlive a civilisation, turning beneath rings of suspended ice and mineral dust.

children.name: Jaunes observation note
children.__text: The Great Spiral has been turning for 9,000 years.

children.name: Devis description
children.__text: At the edge of the blue light lies Devis, a pale archive of the system’s first winter. Vast crystalline plains conceal a dark, warm ocean beneath forty kilometres of ice.

children.name: Devis observation note
children.__text: A frozen surface. An unexpected world underneath.

backgroundImage.altText: Devis, a white ice world split by blue crystalline fissures.

children.name: Indy description
children.__text: Indy keeps a quiet watch over Devis. Silver impact basins hold ancient blue ice, and its slow, synchronised orbit always offers the same scarred face to the planet it calls home.

children.name: Indy observation note
children.__text: The smallest world in our atlas. The oldest stories.

backgroundImage.altText: Indy, the silver cratered moon of Devis.

children.name: The blue heart
children.__text: Every world beginswith a little light.

children.name: System introduction
children.__text: One blue hypergiant. Three extraordinary planets. One silent moon. A journey through a system that exists only beyond imagination.

children.name: Fictional universe note
children.__text: A FICTIONAL UNIVERSE. A REAL SENSE OF WONDER.

children.name: Fabre statement
children.__text: Where the ocean learned to glow.

children.name: Fabre description
children.__text: An endless cobalt sea, threaded with living light. Beneath Fabre’s pearl-white storms, luminous reef forests follow the slow pulse of Aetherium across the water.

children.name: Fabre observation note
children.__text: At night, the shoreline becomes a constellation of its own.

backgroundImage.altText: Fabre, a sapphire ocean planet with luminous coastlines.
Jaunes, a turquoise gas giant with immense swirling storms.

children.name: Jaunes statement
children.__text: A world without a still moment.

children.name: Jaunes description
children.__text: Teal cloud rivers circle a world with no solid shore. On Jaunes, a single storm can outlive a civilisation, turning beneath rings of suspended ice and mineral dust.

children.name: Jaunes observation note
children.__text: The Great Spiral has been turning for 9,000 years.

children.name: Devis description
children.__text: At the edge of the blue light lies Devis, a pale archive of the system’s first winter. Vast crystalline plains conceal a dark, warm ocean beneath forty kilometres of ice.

children.name: Devis observation note
children.__text: A frozen surface. An unexpected world underneath.

backgroundImage.altText: Devis, a white ice world split by blue crystalline fissures.

children.name: Indy description
children.__text: Indy keeps a quiet watch over Devis. Silver impact basins hold ancient blue ice, and its slow, synchronised orbit always offers the same scarred face to the planet it calls home.

children.name: Indy observation note
children.__text: The smallest world in our atlas. The oldest stories.

backgroundImage.altText: Indy, the silver cratered moon of Devis.
